ADDED i1: Tests for {@link JsonSetter.Value}, the helper class that captures the {@code nulls} / {@code contentNulls} settings of a {@link JsonSetter} annotation and supp
ADDED i2: Sample annotated field used to verify that a {@link JsonSetter.Value} can be built from a real annotation instance via reflection.
ADDED i3: The canonical "no overrides" value: both null-handling settings are {@link Nulls#DEFAULT}.
ADDED i4: An empty Value leaves both null-handling settings at their defaults...
ADDED i5: ...is associated with the JsonSetter annotation type...
ADDED i6: ...and reports no non-default settings.
ADDED i7: toString() should spell out both null-handling settings.
ADDED i9: equals(): reflexive, but never equal to null or to an unrelated type.
ADDED i11: Building from a real annotation preserves its nulls / contentNulls settings.
ADDED i13: construct(null, null) normalizes to defaults, returning the shared EMPTY instance.
ADDED i14: forContentNulls() sets only the content-nulls setting; value-nulls stays default.
ADDED i15: forValueNulls() sets only the value-nulls setting; content-nulls stays default.
ADDED i16: withContentNulls / withValueNulls each layer a single setting onto the value.
ADDED i17: Passing null is a no-op that returns the same (unchanged) instance.
ADDED i18: Setting a real content-nulls value produces a changed instance...
ADDED i19: ...and re-setting the identical value returns the same instance.
ADDED i20: Layering a value-nulls setting yields a distinct value, unequal to the original.
ADDED i21: withValueNulls(null, null) resets both settings back to default.
ADDED i22: Resetting an already-default value again returns the same instance.
ADDED i23: Overriding the default value with withValueSkip yields an equal-but-distinct instance.
